name: Leaf Margin
desc: A herbarium sheet of leaves caught mid-morphogenesis — each lamina swells out of its primordium, new teeth are inserted into the margin as it lengthens and every tooth drags a secondary vein out to meet it, then chlorophyll drains from the edge inward while the veins hold green, and the spent leaf abscises and tumbles off the sheet.

energy.doc: life-cycle rate + flutter/rock amplitude on the sheet

density.doc: how many specimens are on the sheet (2 at 0 -> 9 at 1)

scale.doc: leaf size vs frame (2.2 = leaves overlap and fill the sheet)

hue.doc: living-chlorophyll hue (senescence always drains toward gold)

teeth.doc: serration depth — entire margin at 0, deeply toothed at 1

lobes.doc: number of lobe pairs — 0 is elliptic/ovate, 3-5 goes oak-like

x.doc: sheet layout shift across the frame

y.doc: sheet layout shift down the frame

style.doc: aesthetic — toned sheet w/ ink margin + banded tonal wash; Atkins photogram (pale mass on Prussian blue); additive translucent radiograph; vein-network-only leaf skeleton over a ghost lamina

seed.doc: seeds the sheet layout, specimen proportions and tooth counts

alpha.doc: opacity of the specimens over the sheet
